title_o: Errors Are Aversive: Defensive Motivation and the Error-Related Negativity
verdict_reason: rp.csv (guid 2hgsk; an identical copy sits in 'analysis code') has 126 rows = 42 participants x 3 startle types with ERN and EPS; the audit script's Pearson correlation on the 'error' rows gives r=-.253, t(40)=-1.65, p=.106, matching the table (r=-.25, p=.11). The data hold 42 participants while the table and the report say 43 (report: 8 of 51 excluded; the data lack 9 ids), a one-person gap the statistic itself confirms (df=40).

data_files.notes: CR-only line endings; long format, ERN and EPS repeated across the 3 startle_type rows per participant; participant ids 1-51 minus 3,4,10,18,20,28,37,40,44; one startle value '???' in an unpred row (not used by the key test)
ERN/EPS pairs, apparently the combined original+replication set used for a secondary analysis; not the key test
ERP waveform exports, not needed for the key test; not opened

key_test.test: Pearson cor.test(ERN, EPS) on rows with startle_type == 'error' (two-sided)

recompute.method: base R cor.test on the downloaded file (the audit script's exact call)

obstacles: N.R=43 and the report's 43 disagree with the 42 participants in the data; the reported r and p are reproduced only with 42
report calls p=.11 one-tailed; it is the two-sided value (one-sided would be .053)
audit script's sample-size line prints nrow(data)=126, not participants
